glossary.meaning: A defined way for software to request data or actions from other software.
The agreed request shape, response shape, errors and behavior of an interface.
A database rule that rejects invalid stored data.
Several operations happening during overlapping time periods.
A group of database changes committed or rolled back together.
Verifying which identity is making a request.
Deciding whether that identity may perform this action on this resource.
A way to associate several requests with an authenticated user.
A rule that must remain true across allowed operations.
Repeating the same logical operation has no additional intended effect.
An external system sends an HTTP notification to your application.
Comparing independent records to find and resolve differences.
A queue holds pending work; a worker executes it separately from the customer request.
Wait longer between retries and vary that delay to spread retry traffic.
A record of work to publish, saved in the same transaction as the business change.
A place for repeatedly failing jobs that require investigation or controlled replay.
A temporary copy of data used to reduce repeated work.
A database structure that accelerates selected queries at storage and write cost.
A versioned change to database structure or stored data.
Using logs, metrics and traces to understand a running system.
Automated checks and a controlled process for preparing and releasing changes.
Targets for acceptable data loss and time to restore service.
Returning application behavior to an earlier known state, where compatible.
The authoritative record for a fact; copies and caches may lag behind.

sources.title: MDN: HTTP overview
sources.note: Network prework and Part 1: requests, responses and the client/server model.

sources.title: MDN: HTTP methods and status codes
sources.note: Part 1: method semantics. Also see the linked MDN HTTP status-code reference.

sources.title: OWASP: Authorization
sources.note: Part 3: deny by default, object ownership and server-side permission checks.

sources.title: OWASP: Session management
sources.note: Security prework and Part 3: sessions, cookie controls and session lifecycle.

sources.title: OWASP: Authentication and recovery
sources.note: Security prework: credential handling and safe authentication behavior.

sources.title: OWASP: REST security and file uploads
sources.note: Security prework and Parts 3 and 8: validation, limits and safe API behavior. File upload companion: cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/File_Upload_Cheat_Sheet.html

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Transactions
sources.note: Part 2: all-or-nothing groups of database changes. Examples are conceptual; use your database documentation.

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Constraints
sources.note: Part 2: primary keys, foreign keys, uniqueness and validation at the data boundary.

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Indexes and isolation
sources.note: Parts 2 and 8: query acceleration and tradeoffs. Isolation companion: postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html

sources.title: Shopify: Product variants
sources.note: Parts 4 and 6: options, sellable variants and inventory. Used as a domain reference, not a required platform.

sources.title: Shopify: Inventory states
sources.note: Parts 4 and 6: distinguish physical stock, commitments and availability. Exact terms vary by platform.

sources.title: Stripe: Webhooks
sources.note: Part 5: signatures, retries, duplicate notifications and ordering. Confirm the chosen provider's actual contract.

sources.title: Stripe: Idempotent requests
sources.note: Part 5: stable request keys and safe retry behavior. Retention windows and API semantics are provider-specific.

sources.title: AWS: Transactional outbox
sources.note: Part 7: persist a business change and pending publication together; make consumers safe for duplicates.

sources.title: AWS: Timeouts, retries and backoff
sources.note: Part 7: bounded retries, jitter and uncertain outcomes after timeouts.

sources.title: OpenTelemetry: Observability concepts
sources.note: Part 9: logs, metrics and traces, with identifiers that connect related work.

sources.title: Playwright: Testing best practices
sources.note: Part 9: verify behavior through independent tests. This is an example testing tool, not a stack requirement.

sources.title: Git: Recording changes
sources.note: Part 10: inspect and record small changes in version control.

sources.title: PostgreSQL: Backup and restore
sources.note: Part 10: backup methods and recovery. Use your host and database procedures, and test restoration.

sources.title: OWASP: Secrets management
sources.note: Parts 3 and 10: limited access, rotation and avoiding credential leaks.
